Among positive results for a rare disease, the absolute number of false positives is often far larger than the true positives. The calculation must use P(B) = P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|not A)P(not A) so that false positives among the negative population are counted in the denominator; looking only at sensitivity badly overestimates the risk.
